# Appeal of Denial — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination**
**Member:** Sawyer Foster
**Member ID:** W558551284
**Reference Number:** POC-64107D6EF7-65599
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-01
**Plan:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield (Commercial/ACA), New Hampshire
**Governing Policy:** Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon), effective 11/05/2023 — https://files.providernews.anthem.com/2519/PDF-Small-Joint-Surgery-2023-11-05.pdf

Dear Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702). My denial notice states that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am asking that you reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me, and I believe the records already in my file meet the plan's own published criteria for this surgery.

## The Plan's Criteria and My Records

The governing policy states that "ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

> "Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint • Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management • Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses) • Device is FDA approved"

Here is how my records address each part of this list:

- **Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint.** My weight-bearing ankle radiographs from 2026-06-05 showed tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts.

- **Significant pain and functional impairment persisting after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management.** I completed 14 weeks (2026-03-09 to 2026-06-15) of supervised physical therapy for ankle strengthening and balance, totaling 18 visits, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also tried NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-16 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. My exam notes an antalgic gait, walking limited to two blocks, positive provocative testing, and range of motion limited by pain. The policy defines "significant pain and functional impairment" as "pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes." My difficulty walking is documented; if a numeric VAS score and any additional impacted activity (such as difficulty wearing shoes) are recorded elsewhere in my chart, I am asking my surgeon's office to supply that documentation: [VAS pain score, if documented] and [second impacted daily activity, if documented].

- **Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion.** I do not see a specific note about pedal pulses in the summary I have. If this was assessed and documented at a visit, I am asking that it be added to the record supporting this appeal: [documentation of pedal pulse/vascular perfusion exam, if performed].

- **Device is FDA approved.** I understand this refers to the specific implant my surgeon plans to use. I am asking my surgeon's office to confirm the device name and its FDA clearance status for the record: [device name and FDA approval/clearance information].

The policy also states, "If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented," and separately, "If conservative management is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such an approach is not reasonable." In my case, conservative management was appropriate and was tried and documented as described above, so I believe this element of the criteria is satisfied by the physical therapy, medication, and injection records already on file.

## Why I Am Asking for Reconsideration

My denial was based on "incomplete documentation" rather than a conclusion that I do not meet the plan's medical necessity criteria. As shown above, the core clinical elements — radiographic findings and a documented course of conservative treatment lasting well beyond three months — are already in my file. I am asking the plan to review this evidence again, and I am working with my surgeon's office to supply the additional pieces noted above (vascular exam findings, VAS pain score/second impacted activity if recorded, and device information) so that the file is complete.

## Request

I am asking Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield to reconsider and approve coverage for the total ankle replacement (CPT 27702) based on the records described above and any supplemental documentation submitted by my surgeon's office.

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-01-28**. I am sending it according to the instructions on my denial letter, which directs appeals to the address printed on that notice; I can also submit through my account at anthem.com, through the Sydney Health app, or by calling the number on my member ID card.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed to complete this review.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Sawyer Foster
Member ID: W558551284
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [Date of submission]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

21 Revision Total Ankle Arthroplasty Revision total ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:
If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented.

Conservative management offered by the provider or other health professionals for this condition(s) should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function:

• Activity modification • Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics • Corticosteroid injection(s) • Debridement of associated hyperkeratotic lesions, such as corns or calluses Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate.
If conservative management is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such an approa ch is not reasonable.

For the purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes.
Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery is strongly recommended.

Where there are patient-specific modifiable comorbidities that may adversely impact patient reported outcomes or the health status of the patient a shared decision-making process with the patient to discuss these modifiable comorbidities is strongly recommended and should be documented.
